name: Elephant
funFact: An African elephant's trunk alone weighs around 130 kg — heavier than most adult humans.

name: Blue whale
funFact: A blue whale's heart is the size of a small car and beats as slowly as 2 times per minute when diving.

name: Bag of sugar
funFact: The average person in a developed country consumes about 38 kg of sugar per year — 38 bags.

name: Chicken
funFact: There are about 3 chickens for every human on Earth — roughly 26 billion chickens alive at any given time.

name: House cat
funFact: Cats spend about 70% of their lives asleep — roughly 16 hours a day.

name: Bowling ball
description: Standard bowling ball mass ≈ 6.35 kg (14 lbs).
funFact: Bowling balls are required to weigh no more than 16 lbs (7.26 kg) — but most serious bowlers use 14–15 lbs.

name: Newborn baby
funFact: The heaviest baby ever born weighed 10.2 kg (22.5 lbs) — in 1879 in Ohio.

name: Golden retriever
funFact: Golden retrievers were originally bred in Scotland in the 1860s as hunting dogs to retrieve waterfowl.

name: Grand piano
funFact: A concert grand piano has around 12,000 individual parts and over 220 strings under a combined tension of about 18 tonnes.

name: Small car
funFact: Cars have gotten heavier by about 25% since the 1980s — mostly due to safety features and larger engines.

name: Rhinoceros
funFact: A rhino's horn is made of keratin — the same protein as human fingernails — and grows continuously throughout its life.

name: Double-decker bus
funFact: The iconic London double-decker Routemaster bus was designed with an open rear platform — and conductors would jump on and off while it was still moving.

name: T-Rex
funFact: Despite its fearsome reputation, T-Rex had tiny arms that could only curl about 180 kg — less than a human bench press per unit of arm size.

name: Space Shuttle
funFact: At launch, the Space Shuttle burned through 3.4 million kg of propellant in just over 8 minutes — roughly one kilogram every millisecond.

name: Paperclip
funFact: A single gram is defined as the mass of 1 cubic centimetre of water at 4°C — the temperature at which water is densest.

name: Grain of rice
description: Single grain of rice mass ≈ 25 mg.
funFact: There are roughly 29,000 grains of rice in a standard 1 kg bag.

name: Eiffel Tower
funFact: The Eiffel Tower expands by up to 17 cm in summer heat — its iron frame acts like a giant thermometer.

name: Feather
funFact: A bald eagle has around 7,000 feathers, yet all of them together weigh less than its skeleton. Feathers are made of keratin — the same protein as human fingernails.

name: Grain of sand
funFact: There are roughly 7.5 quintillion grains of sand on Earth's beaches — more than all the stars in the observable universe. Yet a single grain weighs about 50 micrograms, less than a human eyelash.

name: Hummingbird
funFact: A hummingbird's heart beats up to 1,260 times per minute during flight — over 20 beats per second. To maintain this, they consume up to twice their body weight in nectar every day.

name: LEGO brick
funFact: A single LEGO 2×4 brick can withstand 432 kg of force before it deforms — meaning a column of 375,000 LEGO bricks stacked on top of each other would be needed before the bottom one gave way. The bricks are tougher than they look.

name: AA battery
funFact: AA batteries have been the same size since 1907. The 'AA' designation comes from the American National Standards Institute and refers to the physical dimensions — nothing to do with power output.

name: Golf ball
funFact: Golf balls have 300–500 dimples, which reduce air drag by up to 50% and allow the ball to travel roughly twice as far as a smooth ball. The dimple pattern was discovered by accident when golfers noticed nicked, battered old balls flew further.

name: Can of soup
exampleMeme: The true unit of pantry weight.
funFact: The tin can was invented in 1810, but the can opener wasn't invented until 1858 — 48 years later. In the interim, the instructions on cans literally said to open with a chisel and hammer.

name: iPhone
funFact: The first iPhone in 2007 weighed 135 g. Modern iPhones are heavier despite advances in materials — because screens got larger and battery capacity roughly tripled. You are literally carrying more energy in your pocket.

name: Human brain
funFact: The human brain is about 1.4 kg — slightly less than a bag of sugar — yet it consumes 20% of your body's total energy. Despite being 2% of body mass, it demands a fifth of every calorie you eat.

name: Litre of water
description: One litre of water = exactly 1 kg.
funFact: The kilogram was originally defined as the mass of one litre of water at 4°C in 1795. For over 200 years it was defined by a physical platinum-iridium cylinder in Paris. In 2019 it was redefined using fundamental constants of physics.

name: Human heart
exampleMeme: Lighter than you'd expect for something so important.
funFact: The human heart weighs about 300 g — less than a can of soup — yet pumps roughly 7,500 litres of blood per day. Over a lifetime it pumps enough blood to fill 3 supertankers.

name: Your skin
description: Total skin mass of an average adult ≈ 4 kg.
exampleMeme: Your largest organ weighs more than your brain.
funFact: Your skin is your heaviest organ at about 4 kg, covering roughly 2 square metres. The outer layer completely replaces itself every 2–3 weeks — you shed about 30,000 dead skin cells per hour, meaning you cycle through roughly a new skin every month.

name: Human skeleton
exampleMeme: The scaffolding inside you weighs less than a laptop.
funFact: Your skeleton accounts for about 15% of your body weight — roughly 5 kg for an average adult. Bones are not rigid permanent structures: the entire skeleton is replaced cell by cell roughly every 10 years.

name: Corgi
funFact: Queen Elizabeth II owned more than 30 corgis over her 70-year reign, almost all descended from Susan — a corgi she received for her 18th birthday. The Queen reportedly insisted on feeding them herself using individually prepared dishes.

name: Labrador retriever
exampleMeme: The most popular dog breed in the world, by weight.
funFact: Labradors have a genetic mutation in the POMC gene that affects the hormone signalling when they are full — meaning many Labradors are literally unable to feel satiated. This makes them highly food-motivated and easy to train, but also prone to obesity.

name: Washing machine
exampleMeme: The heaviest thing most people try to move alone.
funFact: A washing machine spin cycle creates forces of up to 1,000 Gs on the clothes inside — the same force experienced by fighter pilots in a tight turn, but sustained for minutes rather than seconds.

name: Great white shark
description: Average adult great white shark ≈ 700 kg.
funFact: Great white sharks can detect a single drop of blood diluted into 100 litres of water — but contrary to popular belief, they do not actively hunt humans. Most attacks are investigative bites; humans are not on their menu.

name: Orca
exampleMeme: The ocean's apex predator. Not a whale.
funFact: Orcas are technically the largest member of the dolphin family, not whales. They hunt in coordinated family groups, using culture passed down through generations — different orca populations have distinct dialects, hunting techniques, and social norms.

name: International Space Station
exampleMeme: The heaviest thing orbiting Earth right now.
funFact: The ISS weighs 420 tonnes yet maintains orbit by travelling at 7.7 km per second — completing 16 orbits of Earth every 24 hours. You can see it with the naked eye on a clear night, moving visibly across the sky.

name: Great Pyramid of Giza
description: Great Pyramid of Giza ≈ 5.9 billion kg.
funFact: The Great Pyramid contains approximately 2.3 million stone blocks weighing on average 2.5 tonnes each. For 3,800 years it was the tallest structure on Earth. Modern engineers still debate exactly how it was built.
